topic: A family member announces they're converting to a different religion

topic: A family member announces they're converting to a different religion

topic: A family member announces they're converting to a different religion

topic: A family member announces they're converting to a different religion

topic: A family member announces they're converting to a different religion

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding

topic: A person runs into their ex at a mutual friend's wedding

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement

topic: An employee is asked to train their replacement

topic: A person's manuscript is rejected by their dream publisher

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else

topic: A musician hears their song being performed by someone else
text: It was at an open mic. A guy I'd never met played my song under a different title. People sang along. I almost stood up. I sat back down. I had registered the copyright; I had the timestamps; I had the tracks. I left without saying anything. The folder where I kept the legal paperwork sat on my desk for weeks. I never opened it again. I told my partner I'd had a long week. He nodded. I did not pick up the guitar that night.

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text: Coach Vega called the kid into his office on a Thursday. The kid had worked harder than anyone. Coach explained the roster math. The kid nodded. He skipped the booster club call. He skipped the next one too. He had been writing a book on coaching philosophy. He stopped working on it. He stopped opening it.

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text: I told her after practice. She was thirteen. She'd been running this drill perfectly for three years. The decision had been made above me, but I was the face of it. topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text: Amir sat across from the parents in a small office. He told them their son hadn't made the cut. He'd watched the boy work for two seasons. He'd taught the boy a hook shot. He left the office with the door open. He drove home the long way. He did not turn on the kitchen light.

topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text: I cut three players this morning. The third was a senior who had captained JV. He didn't argue. He just asked if there was anything he could have done. topic: A coach has to cut a player from the team
text: Karen rehearsed the speech for an hour. In the room, she said something different and shorter. The girl thanked her for the season. The girl's mother sent a polite email later that night. The capstone tournament she had been planning, the one she'd built around this senior class, no longer felt like a thing she had energy to organize. She emailed the assistant coach to take over logistics. She did not look at the schedule again.

topic: A tenant receives an eviction notice
text: The notice was taped to my door in a yellow envelope. I didn't open it for four hours. I knew what it said. The legal aid line had a four-week wait. I did not request a hearing. I did not call my brother. The plan I'd been making to repaint the kitchen, to hang a curtain rod over the radiator, to make this place mine, has gone soft and unfeasible. I sat on the floor with the envelope and watched my cat watch a fly. I didn't move.

topic: A tenant receives an eviction notice
text: Theresa read the notice in the laundromat parking lot. She had been one month late on rent twice in two years. The notice cited 'lease violations' she did not recognize. She did not call the landlord. She did not call the legal aid number. She drove home and sat in the car for twenty minutes. She did not unload the laundry. She brought one basket up. She left the rest in the trunk. She did not unpack it that night. She did not unpack it the next.

topic: A tenant receives an eviction notice
text: I have thirty days. I have six hundred dollars. I have a child in second grade who likes the maple tree outside her window. I told her we might 'go on an adventure.' I do not know what I meant. I did not call her father. I did not call my mother. The list I'd been keeping of free legal clinics was stuck to the fridge. I took it down. I did not throw it out. It is in a drawer with old menus and old keys and old pictures.

topic: A tenant receives an eviction notice
text: When Marcus opened the envelope, he set it down on the counter and stood there for a while. He had been in the unit for nine years. He had a vegetable garden out back that the landlord had pretended not to notice. He turned off the kitchen light. He did not eat dinner. He did not water the plants on the porch. The next morning the basil had wilted. He looked at it. He did not water it. He went to work. He came home. The basil stayed wilted.

topic: A tenant receives an eviction notice
text: The notice arrived on a Wednesday. I am sixty-one. I have lived here since the building was rent-stabilized and the elevator was unreliable. The owner has a buyer. I do not have a fight. I have a cousin in New Jersey who said I could stay 'for a bit.' I did not call her back. I did not start packing. I did not water the plants. I did not call the friend who had offered to help me organize my files. The files have stayed where they were.

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text: Janet found out from a neighbor who said it casually over the fence. Then she Googled it. The articles were old; the photos were grainy. Her bedroom had been a bedroom then, too. She did not tell her husband at first. When she did, he wanted to research mitigation, sage, blessings, paint colors. She nodded along. She did not paint. The house had been her dream for two years. She started leaving lights on in rooms she wasn't in. She stopped saying 'home' aloud.

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text: I learned about it from a podcast a friend recommended. Not knowing it was about my house. I paused at minute eleven. I closed the app. I did not finish the episode. I stopped going down to the basement. I stopped using the back stairs. I had been planning a renovation. I had a binder of countertop samples. I closed the binder. I have not opened it in eight weeks. I told my contractor we were 'reassessing.' I told my husband the same. I have stopped reassessing.

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text: Hector found the articles on a public records website. He read them in his kitchen at midnight. The previous owner had not disclosed; in his state, they hadn't been required to. Hector did not call his lawyer. He did not list the house. The market was bad. He sat in the kitchen until the coffee maker clicked off automatically. He had imagined growing old here. He stopped saying that. He stopped saying anything about the house's future. He started keeping the front porch light on all night, every night.

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text: An old detective stopped by, unannounced, asking if we'd had any 'unusual activity.' I said no. He apologized for the intrusion. After he left, I sat in the foyer. I did not move for an hour. The house was not what I had bought, or maybe it was, and I had bought it without knowing. I did not tell my partner that night. I did not tell him the next night. I have stopped imagining holidays here. I have stopped imagining anything inside these walls at all.

topic: A homeowner learns their house was a former crime scene
text: Aisha learned about it the way you learn about things now: a comment under a Zillow listing she had idly opened. She closed the laptop. She did not tell her husband. She had wanted this house for ten years. She started avoiding the master bedroom in the late afternoons. She moved her reading chair to the hallway. She did not host the housewarming she had planned. She told friends she was 'too busy.' She was not too busy. She just had nothing to celebrate anymore.

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text: I came outside and the driveway was empty. I called the police. They told me to call the towing company. The towing company said the HOA had ordered it. The HOA said someone had complained. The car is still there, somewhere, accruing fees. I have stopped doing the math.

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text: Kim looked out the kitchen window for her car and saw two empty rectangles of dry pavement. She called the non-emergency line. She called the company. The fees added up faster than she could write them down. She wrote them down anyway. Then she stopped writing. She did not file a complaint with the city. She did not call her insurance. She had been driving for the rideshare app on weekends to save for her son's braces. She cancelled the appointment. She did not reschedule.

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text: I had three weeks left on the loan. I came outside to drive to the credit union and pay it off. The driveway was empty. The tow had been ordered by mistake; the dispatcher said sorry on the phone in a tone that meant nothing would happen. I sat in the kitchen. I did not call the credit union. I did not pay the loan that month. The penalty added up. I let it. I have stopped paying things on time. I am late on everything. I am late on myself.

topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text: Carl learned his truck had been towed when he stepped onto the porch with his coffee. He stood there a long time. He had bought the truck used, two months ago. He had named it for his grandfather. The HOA cited a dispute over property lines that had been unresolved for years. Carl did not engage. He took the bus to work. topic: A person's car is towed from their own driveway
text: It happened twice. The first time, my landlord apologized. The second time, my landlord said it was the new owner's policy. I had been planning to install a charger for my new EV. topic: A neighbor's tree falls on their property
text: When the oak came down in the storm, it took the back fence and the garden shed. Linda stood in the yard the next morning in her bathrobe. The neighbor came over with apologies. topic: A neighbor's tree falls on their property
text: The neighbor's pine cracked through my roof at 3 a.m. We're fine. The cat is fine. The insurance adjuster said it would take eight weeks at minimum. The contractor my brother recommended said sixteen. I sat on the front step. I did not call. I did not call my husband at his conference. I have stopped initiating calls. I have asked my neighbor for nothing; I am not going to ask. The hole in the roof has a tarp. I have stopped looking up. The ceiling can have its own weather.

topic: A neighbor's tree falls on their property
text: Vince walked the perimeter of his property after the maple fell. The branches had crushed his greenhouse. The greenhouse had been a five-year project. He had been growing tomatoes for the farmer's market. He did not call the market. He did not call his cousin who had helped him build the frame. He sat in a folding chair. He did not move it inside when it began to rain. The rain did not bother him. He had stopped, generally, making sure things were dry. He just let things be wet.

topic: A neighbor's tree falls on their property
text: I was awake when it happened. I heard it for what it was; I did not need to look. In the morning, the magnolia I had planted with my late husband was buried under the neighbor's elm. The neighbor sent a text apologizing. He used too many exclamation points. I did not reply. The magnolia might survive. I cannot bring myself to ask the arborist. I cancelled the appointment. I have stopped tending the front bed. The mulch will need turning. I will not turn it this season.

topic: A neighbor's tree falls on their property
text: Mike heard the impact before he saw it. The neighbor's spruce took out the dog run and the section of fence that bordered the alley. The dog had been inside; that was the small mercy. topic: Someone discovers their neighbor is secretly wealthy

topic: Someone discovers their neighbor is secretly wealthy
text: Greg discovered his neighbor's wealth on accident; a property record search at work surfaced a name he recognized. He didn't say anything at the block party that weekend. topic: Someone discovers their neighbor is secretly wealthy
text: She lent me twenty dollars last month for the bake sale. I paid it back with interest as a joke. topic: Someone discovers their neighbor is secretly wealthy
text: Camille saw the magazine spread by accident. She stopped inviting them to dinner. She made up reasons. The reasons piled up. The dinners stopped, and nobody asked why.

topic: Someone discovers their neighbor is secretly wealthy
text: I learned through a gossip column that the man who fixes my mailbox out of kindness owns a hedge fund. I sat in the front seat of my car. The world I had been measuring myself against was the wrong size. I have been saving for a fence for eighteen months. I cancelled the contractor's visit. The fence was going to be the project; the project was the proof I was making it. There is no it. There is only a yard, and a row of expensive houses I do not understand.

topic: A student learns their scholarship application was denied
text: Tomas opened the email at the public library, where the Wi-Fi was free. The denial was polite. He had needed this scholarship for his second-year tuition. He logged off. topic: A student learns their scholarship application was denied
text: I read the email three times. The committee thanked me for my application. I closed the laptop. I had spent two months on the personal statement. I had paid a stranger fifty dollars to edit it. I cancelled the campus visit I'd booked for next week. I cancelled the meeting with the financial aid office. I have stopped opening emails from the school. I told my dad I was 'figuring it out.' I am not figuring it out. I am sitting still and pretending it counts.

topic: A student learns their scholarship application was denied
text: When Yuki saw the denial, she put her phone face down on her bed. She did not move for an hour. She had been the first in her family to even apply. Her mother asked if she was okay. Yuki said the rice was overcooked. The rice was fine.

topic: A student learns their scholarship application was denied
text: The decision came at 4:47 p.m. I had refreshed the portal every hour. I closed the tab. I did not tell my mom. The campus tour I had planned to take next month, the one my dad had bought a plane ticket for, I quietly cancelled. I told him my schedule had changed. He didn't push. I think he could hear it. topic: A student learns their scholarship application was denied
text: Marcus refreshed the portal until the words finalized. The denial blurred. He did not tell his coach. He did not tell his sister. He had been writing essays since the summer. topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: The professor scheduled the meeting in vague language. In her office, she showed me the report. The numbers said sixty-seven percent. I tried to explain the way I write, the way I draft. The major I had loved, the cohort I had eaten lunch with, became a hallway I avoided. I have stopped raising my hand. I have stopped sitting in the front row.

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: When the email arrived from academic affairs, Maya read it twice and walked to the dining hall. She didn't eat. She had used her own work from a previous class; the system had flagged it. She skipped class on Tuesday. She emailed her TA that she was 'unwell.' The TA didn't ask follow-ups.

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: The accusation came from a paper I had cited correctly, but the professor's database disagreed. The hearing scheduled itself like weather. I did not gather evidence. I did not ask my friends to write character letters. I did not, in fact, do anything. I sat through the hearing. They asked me questions. I answered most of them. I did not answer one. The decision came two weeks later. By then I had stopped attending the class. I had stopped attending the major. I had stopped attending myself.

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: Daniel was called into the dean's office on a Wednesday. The TA had flagged his code. The code was his. Daniel said this. The dean nodded and said the process would 'play out.' Daniel left the office and walked to the engineering building and sat at a bench until it grew cold. He did not contact the TA. He did not contact his friends in the class. He stopped opening Piazza. He stopped doing the assignments. He went to lecture and did not take notes. The notebook stayed shut on his desk.

topic: A student is accused of plagiarism
text: She accused me in front of the class. She said she'd send the report. I did not say anything. I did not say I had cited everything; I did not say I had written it on the bus, on a Sunday, with my grandmother dying in another time zone. I went home. I did not write the appeal letter the writing center had offered to help me with. I cancelled the appointment. I have stopped emailing professors. topic: A student receives a much lower grade than expected
text: Liu opened the gradebook and stared at the C-. He had expected an A. He did not refresh. He did not go to office hours. He did not email the professor. He had been considering a graduate program in this field. He closed the application tab. He did not bookmark it. He went to the library and sat in his usual seat. He did not open his books. He scrolled his phone for two hours. He did not study for next week's exam. The exam was three days away.

topic: A student receives a much lower grade than expected
text: The grade was a D. I had thought a B-, maybe lower, but a D rearranged the year. I closed my laptop. I did not eat dinner. I did not call my parents. I did not, the next morning, go to class. I sent the professor an email asking nothing in particular. He replied kindly. I did not write back. The major map I'd taped to my wall came down that weekend. I did not put another map up. I have stopped mapping. I sit at my desk and look at the wall.

topic: A student receives a much lower grade than expected
text: Pri's transcript update appeared at midnight. The B+ on her thesis was lower than she'd been led to expect. The advisor had called her work 'strong' in March. The grade did not match. She did not write to her advisor. She did not request feedback. She went to bed. She did not sleep. The PhD applications she had been drafting on a separate hard drive stayed on the hard drive. She did not move the files. She did not delete them. She just stopped opening them. The drive sat on her desk.

topic: A student receives a much lower grade than expected
text: I worked harder on this paper than on any paper I have ever written. The grade was a C. The comments were brief. I read them twice and then stopped. I did not request a regrade. I did not bring it up in class. I did not bring it up with my study group. I have not opened the assignment portal in two weeks. I have stopped checking my grades, in general. I will see them at the end. I will see them whether I check or not.

topic: A student receives a much lower grade than expected
text: Eli got back the midterm with a 47 in red. He folded the paper without flinching. He had stayed up three nights for that exam. He did not go to the review session. He did not meet with the TA. He sat in the dining hall and ate alone. The grad school list he kept in his planner stayed where it was, but he stopped adding to it. He stopped reading the schools' websites. He stopped saying the names out loud. He went to class. He went to bed early. He didn't dream.

topic: A person finds out they were adopted through a DNA test
text: The result came up on a Sunday morning while I was eating cereal. Zero percent match with my dad. A long pause as the bowl got soggy. I closed the laptop. I did not call my mother. I did not call my brother. I called nobody. I have a journal where I keep family stories I want to write down for my kids. I closed the journal. I have not written in it in two months. I have stopped telling my children stories about their grandparents. The stories don't belong to me.

topic: A person finds out they were adopted through a DNA test
text: Henry took the test as a Christmas present from his daughter. The results came after New Year's. He sat in the kitchen and read them three times. He did not bring it up at dinner. He did not bring it up the next dinner. He told his wife he had a headache. The album of family photos he had been digitizing for his grandchildren sat in the basement. He stopped scanning. He stopped at 1973. He did not open the box of older photos. The box stayed on the shelf, dusted lightly.

topic: A person finds out they were adopted through a DNA test
text: I match thirty-seven cousins on my father's side, none of whom share his last name. The pattern is not subtle. I did not confront my father. I did not confront my mother. I made dinner. I asked about their week. I have stopped asking about my own. The genealogy project I have been chairing in our community has me sitting in front of family trees I can no longer read with confidence. I stepped down. I told them I needed to focus on family. I did not specify which one.

topic: A person finds out they were adopted through a DNA test
text: Rosa learned the truth at forty-two. She did not respond to the matched relative who had reached out. She closed the app. She did not delete the account. She just left it suspended in the way you leave something you cannot decide about. She stopped attending family Sunday lunches. She told her mother she had work. The work was the lie. The lie was easier than the truth, and the truth was unraveling faster than she could keep up with. She bought a smaller calendar and didn't fill it in.

topic: A person finds out they were adopted through a DNA test
text: I had taken the kit for fun. The fun ended at the second sentence of the report. My mother is not biologically my mother. The piece of furniture inside me where my history sat was empty, suddenly, like a room I had been picturing for years. I did not call her. I did not call my sister. I cancelled the family vacation I had been planning for the summer. I told everyone I had work. I have stopped saying anything else. I am very, very tired of words.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: The DNA app pinged with a 'half-sister' match. Marcus sat on the bus. He did not click on her profile. He let the notification sit until it disappeared into the others. He had thought of his father as a fixed thing. The fixed thing had a hidden side. He did not call his mother. He did not call his sister. He did not tell his wife. He closed the app. He kept his hands in his pockets the rest of the ride. He did not order takeout that night. He skipped dinner.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: Her name is Hannah. She lives in Texas. She sent me a message that began 'this is going to sound strange.' I closed the app. I have not replied. I had been planning a memoir of my father, who died last year. I closed the document. I cannot finish a memoir of someone I did not, apparently, know. I told my editor we needed to push the deadline. He said he understood. He didn't, but his understanding was less important than the way the project had become weightless in my hands.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: Sasha discovered the half-brother on a Tuesday. He was thirty-one and lived two miles away. She had walked past his apartment for years. She did not message him. She did not message her father. She did not tell her therapist at the next session. The framed family photos in her hallway looked the same and did not feel the same. She took one down to clean the glass and then did not rehang it. She put it on the shelf. She closed the closet door. She washed her hands.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: He is a year older than me. He has my eyes, in pictures online. I do not know what to do with this. I have not told my mother. I have not told my husband. I told the dog, in a way, by sitting next to her too long. The family album project I had been making for my mother's seventieth birthday is on hold. I told my sister we needed to 'rethink the format.' I have stopped thinking about it altogether. I have stopped thinking about a lot of things.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: When the message came in, Diane read it standing up at the sink. She did not respond. She did not screenshot. She continued doing the dishes. The brother in the message was older than she was. She skipped the reunion. She told her cousins her flight had been cancelled. She did not look at flights again.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: The article was long. The evidence was specific. The author I had quoted in toasts and tattoos and college essays had taken sentences whole from a writer I had never heard of. I put them in a box in the closet, behind the holiday decorations. I have stopped recommending books in general. I do not trust the part of me that recommends.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: Selena read the expose in two sittings. She had read every novel by him. She had been to two readings. She had quoted him in her wedding vows. After the article, she did not finish the cup of tea she had made. The reread project she had been planning for the fall, his entire backlist, evaporated in twenty minutes. She did not announce the cancellation. She did not tell anyone. She just stopped pulling the books off the shelf. The shelf stayed how it was. She walked past it without looking.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: I named my daughter after a character of his. I read the article on my phone in the school pickup line. I sat in the car after I parked. I did not get out for a while. I did not say anything to my husband that night. I did not say anything to my daughter. I have stopped using her middle name as a nickname. I tell myself this is normal at her age. topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: When the news broke, Aaron was at the bookstore. He put the new release back on the table. He left without buying anything. He did not order anything online for a month. He had been planning to write a tribute essay for his blog about the author's tenth novel. He closed the draft. He did not delete it. He just let it sit. The blog stayed quiet. He stopped checking his analytics. He stopped checking the comments. He had less to say about books, generally, after that week.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: I wrote my college essay about him. I cited him. I got into school partly because of him. I read the article and felt the year I had been making fall in on itself. I did not return the books. I did not delete the post on my blog. I did, however, stop reading. Not just him. All of it. I had a stack of novels by my bed. I moved them to the floor. I moved them to a closet. topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: The gate agent announced another delay at 9:14 p.m. Mira's brother's wedding was at noon the next day, two thousand miles away. She did not call her brother. She did not call her parents. topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: I missed my mother's seventieth because of weather in Atlanta. They held the cake until eleven. I told them not to. I sat in the airport hotel and ate eggs by myself the next morning. I did not catch the next flight. I rebooked for a Wednesday and then cancelled it. I told her I would come 'soon.' Soon has been a word in my mouth for so long now that it has lost its meaning. I have stopped putting dates around my visits home.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: Joshua's connection got delayed by twelve hours. He missed the keynote he was supposed to deliver. He did not refresh the airline app. He sat on the floor by the gate and watched a child eat french fries. He did not call the conference organizer. He did not check his email. The keynote was the talk he had been working toward for six years. He did not file a claim. He did not request a credit. He boarded a plane home a day later. He did not unpack.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: I was supposed to be at my best friend's funeral. The plane sat on the tarmac for four hours. By the time we took off, the service was over. I sat in the airport in Charlotte and ate a salad I did not taste. I did not call her husband. I did not call her sister. I sent a text. I deleted it before sending. I have not reached out since. I had been planning to give a reading at the memorial. I have closed the document. I will not give the reading.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: Claire's flight was delayed eight hours. She missed her daughter's high school graduation. She watched the livestream on her phone in a Hudson News. The Wi-Fi cut out at the speeches. She did not boost it with the airport pass. She did not text her ex-husband to record it. She got on the next flight. She did not bring her daughter the gift she had wrapped. She left it at the gate, by accident, then on purpose. She did not return for it. The gate cleaned up at midnight.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: The dog is back. I am not sure how. The fence has been repaired three times. I have called animal control twice. I have called the neighbor four times. The neighbor says she 'doesn't know how it happens.' I stopped calling. I stopped repairing. I cancelled the landscaping appointment because the dog had dug up the new beds. I have not replanted. The yard is the dog's now, in the way that things become the things that take them. I sit on the back porch and watch.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: Carl found the dog in his vegetable garden again at 6 a.m. He carried the dog home. He did not knock. He left the dog tied to the porch with a soft note. The neighbor sent a long apology by text. Carl did not respond. He came home that evening to find the dog back in his yard. He stopped trying to deliver it. He fed it leftover chicken. He did not contact the HOA. He did not contact the police. The vegetable garden was in tatters. He did not replant. He did not even till.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: I have a baby. The dog gets out twice a week. The dog is not aggressive, but it is large. I have asked, kindly. I have asked, firmly. I have asked, in writing. Nothing changes. I have stopped letting my daughter play in the yard. I have stopped putting her down on the back lawn. I have stopped imagining the swing set we bought before she was born. The swing set is still in the box, in the garage, behind the bicycles I no longer ride.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: Anna was up to ten escape incidents in two months. The neighbor remained polite and unaccountable. Anna stopped logging the incidents in her notebook. She had been considering legal action. She did not call the lawyer. She did not, in fact, do anything. She bought a chair for the back porch and stopped using the back porch. She let the back gate stay closed. The dog wandered, and so did her plans for the lawn party she had imagined since moving in.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: I have to walk the dog home now. I know its name. I know the neighbor's name. I have stopped knowing what to do. I take the dog back. I knock. The neighbor smiles. The neighbor closes the door. The dog will be back tomorrow. I have stopped buying mulch. I have stopped pretending the back garden is mine. I sit inside in the afternoons. I close the blinds. I have given up on the part of the house that points outward, gently and completely.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: Ben hit send before he saw the wrong name in the recipient field. The text was about his boss. The recipient was his boss. He stared at the bubble until it turned blue with 'read.' He did not type. He did not unsend. He went to the bathroom. He came back. He did not eat lunch. He did not eat dinner. He went to bed at eight. He had been preparing for a promotion review. He stopped reviewing his deck. He cancelled the prep meeting. He did not reschedule it. He just let it disappear.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: I sent it to him. The text was about him. He read it within thirty seconds. He did not reply. The relationship I had been building for a year, the easy lunches, the inside joke about the bagel place, all sat in a different shape now, like furniture rearranged in the dark. I did not apologize. I cancelled coffee on Friday. He didn't ask why. I think he knows. I think we both know. The friendship is not coming back, and I am not, this time, trying to bring it.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: Carol sent a complaint about her sister to her sister. She tried to delete the message; her sister had iOS that didn't support deletion. She typed an explanation, then deleted it. She typed an apology, then deleted it. She did not send anything. She watched her phone the rest of the night. The message stayed read. The reply did not come. She missed her sister's birthday call the next week. She told her mother she had been busy. She had not been busy. She had simply stopped picking up.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: I sent the photo to a coworker instead of my partner. The photo was personal. It was not bad. It was not for him. He has not said anything. I have not said anything. I have not been in the room with him alone since. The promotion track I had been planning, the dinner with his boss next month, the cross-team project we were going to pitch, has gone soft in the way these things go soft. I cancelled the dinner. I did not propose another. I have stopped proposing.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: Ravi accidentally texted his ex-wife instead of his current partner. The text was a long, vulnerable paragraph about the partner. The ex-wife replied with two question marks. He did not explain. He set his phone on the kitchen counter and walked out of the room. He did not pick the phone up for hours. The current partner came home and asked about dinner. Ravi said he had not started dinner. They ordered out. He did not eat. He did not, that week, write any more long paragraphs.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: When the email arrived from the president, Stephanie stood at the kitchen counter in her bathrobe. She read it twice. The college had been her plan since seventh grade. She did not refresh. She did not call her advisor. She did not call her parents. She turned off her phone. She did not log into class that day. She did not log into class the next. The transfer fairs the email mentioned were happening on Friday. She did not register. She lay on her back on the floor and looked at the ceiling for a long time.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: I have one semester left. They are not letting us finish. The teach-out plan is half-finished and the receiving school is across the country. I have not opened the FAQ. I have not registered for the meeting. I have stopped going to my classes. The professors understand, kind of. They are also leaving. I cancelled my graduation announcements; my mother had pre-ordered fifty. I told her to return them. She offered to keep them anyway, 'for later.' I asked her not to.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: Andre got the news at his work-study job. He kept doing inventory. He did not pause. The inventory took him an extra hour because he was moving slowly. He went home and did not tell his roommate. He sat on his bed. He had been the first in his family. He did not call his mother. He did not call his counselor. He did not look at the transfer school list. He did not look at anything. He charged his phone and did not unlock it.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: The press release came out at 4 p.m. The campus newspaper site crashed. I refreshed it twice and then stopped. I have been the editor of that paper. I did not run an issue about the closure. I did not assign anyone. I went to a movie alone. I cancelled the editorial meeting. The senior thesis I had been writing, on the founding of this school, sat in my drive untouched. I have not opened it. I will not. The founding does not matter when the closing is also written.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: Laura had picked her college because of its small classes. The closure announcement listed three transfer partners. None of them had small classes. She did not request transcripts. She did not attend the town hall. She skipped the rest of her seminar that semester. The thesis advisor she had been waiting six months to work with sent a kind email. She did not respond. She started spending afternoons in the library reading novels. She did not check out any of them. She put them back on the shelf at closing time.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: The diagnosis was not mine. The medications were not mine. The treatment plan I had been following for three months was not for me. I sat in the doctor's office, and the doctor said sorry, and I said okay. I did not file a complaint. I did not call the patient advocate. I went home and threw the pill bottles in a bag. I did not throw them out. The bag has sat by the door for two weeks. I have stopped opening the door fully when I leave.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: Oren learned about the mix-up at a follow-up appointment. The nurse apologized. The doctor apologized. He did not ask the questions he had written down. He did not pull the list out of his pocket. He went home. He cancelled the second opinion he had been planning. He cancelled the work-from-home accommodation he had requested for treatments he had not actually needed. He did not call HR. He did not call his ex-wife to tell her. He did not call anyone. He sat in the kitchen and listened to the refrigerator.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: It turns out the lump on the scan was someone else's. The diagnosis I had been carrying for two months was not mine. The relief did not come the way it should have. The trust I had in the system, the doctors, the chain of evidence, did not bounce back. I cancelled the second appointment. I cancelled the consultation. I have stopped looking at the patient portal. I have stopped, frankly, looking at my body. I am very tired of being a body that other people read incorrectly.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: Haya found out that her records had been merged with another patient's of the same name. The other patient's history included three surgeries and a chronic condition. Haya's history did not. The hospital said it would 'unmerge' over the next quarter. Haya did not refresh the portal. She did not call the records office. She did not, in fact, call anyone. She let the appointment for her annual physical pass. She did not reschedule. She put the pill bottles she had been mistakenly prescribed into a paper bag and put the bag on the porch.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: The doctor told me I did not have what they had said I had. He smiled. He thought I would smile back. I sat there. I had told my children. I had told my employer. I had told my closest friends. The story I had been telling about myself, dying, surviving, fighting, was not my story. I have not corrected anyone. I have stopped telling stories about myself entirely. I drove home. I did not call my children. The phone has been on silent for a long time now.
